newsitem.title: USA: N.J. prison legislation could cost $2 bln -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. prison legislation could cost $2 bln -- paper.

text.p: A bill sailing through the New Jersey Legislature to limit parole could cost as much as $2 billion to implement, the Bergen Record reported Tuesday.
The Assembly Appropriations Committee approved the measure Monday, and the state Senate has already approved a similar bill without a single dissenting vote.

The measure would require violent offenders to serve at least 85 percent of their sentences before becoming eligible for parole. Inmates targeted by the bill currently serve about 42 percent of their sentences, the newspaper said.
The bill would require the state to build at least one new prison at a cost of $390 million, and spend $107 million annually in operating costs, according to the state Corrections Department.
The Department said overcrowding at state prisons already would require $355 million in construction projects to fix, not including the impact resulting from passage of the parole bill.
